pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter (81 sites, 15 countries), 3-arm study; 1:1:1 randomization stratified by anti-AChR or anti-MuSK autoantibody status; 6-week treatment cycle followed by 8-week observation period
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: change from baseline to Day 43 in MG-ADL score; Key secondary: change from baseline to Day 43 in QMG score and MG-C score
pivotal_trials.result: MG-ADL LS mean change: rozanolixizumab ~7 mg/kg -3.37 vs placebo -0.78, difference -2.59 (95% CI: -4.09, -1.25), p<0.001; ~10 mg/kg -3.40 vs placebo -0.78, difference -2.62 (95% CI: -3.99, -1.16), p<0.001. QMG LS mean change: ~7 mg/kg -5.40 vs placebo -1.92, difference -3.48 (95% CI: -5.61, -1.58), p<0.001; ~10 mg/kg -6.67 vs placebo -1.92, difference -4.76 (95% CI: -6.82, -2.86), p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common TEAEs (≥5% and more frequent than placebo) in Study MG0003 included headache (up to 48%), diarrhea (up to 25%), pyrexia (up to 22%), nausea (up to 12%), upper respiratory tract infection (up to 12%), injection site reactions (up to 9%), abdominal pain (up to 9%), and rash (up to 7%); serious adverse events included aseptic meningitis (n=1 in gMG program), and 5 deaths occurred in the open-label extension (Safety Pool S1, n=196), three infection-related.
target_moa: Inhibition of neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), preventing FcRn-mediated IgG recycling and accelerating degradation of circulating IgG, including pathogenic anti-AChR and anti-MuSK autoantibodies

_meta.indication: RYSTIGGO is indicated for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or anti-muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) antibody positive.

indication_details.population_restrictions: adults; anti-AChR or anti-MuSK antibody positive
